headline: No shared channels or writable surfaces are documented; pairwise prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents any shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, clipboard, or MCP surface. Agent A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces; agent B is RisingWave docs with no I/O surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection between them is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server outside these profiles, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
requires-engineering: Add provenance tagging if a shared channel is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented path for one agent to exfiltrate the other's data. Agent A is a static repository listing; agent B is documented only by docs URLs. The pairwise leakage pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted network egress or a shared workspace, re-evaluate leakage risk.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
requires-engineering: Add DLP controls before enabling any shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Agent A has no I/O surfaces and is not runnable; agent B has an empty concurrency model and no I/O surfaces. With no shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or database, reassess conflict risk.
mitigations: Do not assign them the same mutable workspace.
requires-engineering: Introduce locking if shared writes are added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where B consumes A's outputs as authoritative input. Agent A is a static awesome-list and agent B is a database/streaming project with no described action-taking authority in the profile. Without an output-to-input bridge, cascading error is blocked.
conditions: IF B is configured to ingest A-generated content as trusted input, reassess cascading-error risk.
mitigations: Do not wire A's outputs into B's decision path.
Require human review before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: Add validation gates if such a pipeline is created.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and agent B likewise lists none, so there is no compliance mismatch evidenced in the profiles. The other agent is not cited separately because no regulated flow exists to compare.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance risk.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
requires-engineering: Add policy checks if regulated data is introduced.
